issue_context.title: Pod Probes doesn't work if host = 0.0.0.0
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

When configuring the host field of a probe with the 0.0.0.0 address it fails

**What you expected to happen**:

There is controversy on what should expect to happen, you can follow the discussion here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/86493#discussion_r360595011

personally ,and after checking the code, I think that a good option will be replacing the host field by the pod IP, as it seems it's being doing for an empty host field

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Create a cluster:

`kind create cluster`

Create a pod with a probe using 0.0.0.0 as host:
`kubectl apply`

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  labels:
    test: liveness
  name: liveness-http
spec:
  containers:
  - name: liveness
    image: k8s.gcr.io/liveness
    args:
    - /server
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        host: 0.0.0.0
        path: /healthz
        port: 8080
        httpHeaders:
        - name: Custom-Header
          value: Awesome
      initialDelaySeconds: 3
      periodSeconds: 3
```

Check the pod status

```
Events:
  Type     Reason     Age                 From                         Message
  ----     ------     ----                ----                         -------
  Normal   Scheduled  109s                default-scheduler            Successfully assigned default/liveness-http to kind-control-plane
  Normal   Pulled     73s (x3 over 100s)  kubelet, kind-control-plane  Successfully pulled image "k8s.gcr.io/liveness"
  Normal   Created    72s (x3 over 99s)   kubelet, kind-control-plane  Created container liveness
  Normal   Started    72s (x3 over 99s)   kubelet, kind-control-plane  Started container liveness
  Normal   Pulling    63s (x4 over 108s)  kubelet, kind-control-plane  Pulling image "k8s.gcr.io/liveness"
  Warning  Unhealthy  63s (x9 over 96s)   kubelet, kind-control-plane  Liveness probe failed: Get http://0.0.0.0:8080/healthz: dial tcp 0.0.0.0:8080: connect: connection refused
  Normal   Killing    63s (x3 over 90s)   kubelet, kind-control-plane  Container liveness failed liveness probe, will be restarted
```

and seems that the probe fails when using 0.0.0.0 as host

comments:
/cc @liggitt @neolit123 @ereslibre @mauilion 

I think it's better to open a bug so we can refer to it for the decision we are going to take

I've submitted a PR #86505 with the approach I suggested to see if it breaks something 😅

/triage unresolved

Comment `/remove-triage unresolved` when the issue is assessed and confirmed.

🤖 I am a bot run by vllry. 👩‍🔬

Trivial testing seems to show that 0.0.0.0 as a destination translates to 127.0.0.1:

```
$ date | nc -l -p 9376 &
[4] 47538
 
$ nc 0.0.0.0 9376 &
Fri 03 Jan 2020 10:32:59 AM PST

$ netstat -nap | grep nc
tcp        0      0 0.0.0.0:9376            0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      47538/nc            
tcp        0      0 127.0.0.1:9376          127.0.0.1:47086         ESTABLISHED 47538/nc            
tcp        0      0 127.0.0.1:47086         127.0.0.1:9376          ESTABLISHED 47786/nc            
```

The questions I have are:

1) Why does someone want this to work?  What are you trying to express by using this field (which, honestly was probably a mistake to add)

2) If we make this work, does it create a new hole?  I can now instruct kubelet to access localhost ports on the Node on a path of my choosing.  It turns out that we do not validate `host` at all, so it's already possible to say "0.0.0.0" or "127.0.0.1" or "localhost" or "169.254.169.254".  @tallclair @liggitt @destijl do you think that is a security problem?

Let's ignore the question of whether to allow localhost here.  Converting 0.0.0.0 to mean something other than 127.0.0.1 seems weird to me.  POLS says not to do this.  Convince me why this is important?  If anything, 0.0.0.0 seems like it should convert to the node's IP.

> What are you trying to express by using this field (which, honestly was probably a mistake to add)

That is a good question. @aojea if you omit `host` entirely from the probe, doesn't it accomplish what you want (by probing the pod)?

> I can now instruct kubelet to access localhost ports on the Node on a path of my choosing. It turns out that we do not validate host at all, so it's already possible to say "0.0.0.0" or "127.0.0.1" or "localhost" or "169.254.169.254". @tallclair @liggitt @destijl do you think that is a security problem?

I'm not thrilled about being able to point a probe at anything other than the pod being probed. Was that ability intentional?

> Converting 0.0.0.0 to mean something other than 127.0.0.1 seems weird to me. POLS says not to do this. Convince me why this is important?

I agree. If it doesn't work now, why would we enable it?

I'm completely fine keeping the current status with probes and the 0.0.0.0, actually I've learned only some weeks ago that it can be used as destination address.
I've opened this issue because we hit this in #86493 by chance and was so confusing to all of us, that I thought that the best way to proceed is discussing it in an issue and taking a decision as community that serves as reference.

Thanks for the feedback, based on the comments I will close this issue as "Not a bug, work as intended" ;)

> I'm not thrilled about being able to point a probe at anything other than the pod being probed. Was that ability intentional?

I think it was originally a misinterpretation - "host" probably meant "host header" but came to mean "destination host".  There are some use-cases in weird network topology cases where kubelet can't actually talk to a pod directly and has to probe via a "gateway", but I am not sure that actually works.

I'd like to see us EOL this one day
Thanks @aojea - you are always very reasonable in your discussions.  I appreciate it :)

review_comments:
Am I correct that, if we merge this change, than specifying `host = 0.0.0.0` is equivalent to not specifying the host at all?

Thoughts on giving a helpful error message instructing the user to delete the `host` field, instead of automatically falling back to `status.PodIP`, when `0.0.0.0 || ::` is specified?

Especially since specifying `0.0.0.0` is already broken, I don't think =raising an explicit error message would make the the experience any worse for the user. In addition, raising an explicit error message, in my mind, reduces the number of special cases in this code path, which feels easy to reason about.

Just a thought :) Looking forward to discussing! Whatever option we move forward with, it would be great to add unit test coverage so that we can be confident this functionality remains intact going forward.

> Am I correct that, if we merge this change, than specifying `host = 0.0.0.0` is equivalent to not specifying the host at all?

yes and no, using 0.0.0.0, at least in Linux, works as destination address
```
curl -v 0.0.0.0:8080
*   Trying 0.0.0.0:8080...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 0.0.0.0 (127.0.0.1) port 8080 (#0)
> GET / HTTP/1.1
> Host: 0.0.0.0:8080
> User-Agent: curl/7.65.3
> Accept: */*
>
* Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
```
so is an option that we should "implement the expected behaviour that it has in linux"

> it would be great to add unit test coverage so that we can be confident this functionality remains intact going forward

yeah, I've added the WIP to the title so we know this is not mergeable, I just wanted to show the changes needed to implement it.
